title: cert_aki_key_id and cert_ski_key_id allocate Vec<u8> unnecessarily
description:
In pkix-path-builder/src/lib.rs:276-307, cert_aki_key_id and cert_ski_key_id return Option<Vec<u8>>, allocating a new Vec for the extension bytes on every call. The only consumer (rank_candidates at line 341) immediately compares the bytes with as_deref() and drops the Vec.

What goes wrong: Each candidate evaluation allocates 1-2 small Vecs (typically 20 bytes each) that are immediately dropped after a byte comparison. For pools with many candidates, this is O(pool_size) needless allocations per rank_candidates call.

The equivalent functions in pkix-revocation/src/signer_discovery.rs (lines 219-258) return Option<OctetString>, which borrows from the parsed Certificate and avoids allocation entirely.

Locations:
- pkix-path-builder/src/lib.rs:276 (cert_aki_key_id returns Vec<u8>)
- pkix-path-builder/src/lib.rs:298 (cert_ski_key_id returns Vec<u8>)

Recommendation: Return Option<&[u8]> (borrowing from the Certificate's parsed extensions) instead of Option<Vec<u8>>, matching the signer_discovery approach. The parsed x509_cert::ext::pkix::AuthorityKeyIdentifier / SubjectKeyIdentifier types hold OctetString values that can be borrowed.
